# algebraic closure　`def.algebraic-closure`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.algebraic-closure)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.algebraic-closure.md)

## Notes · **stale**
⭐ Examples: $\mathbb{C}$ is an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{R}$; $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ (all algebraic numbers over $\mathbb{Q}$) is an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$; an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{F}_p$ is $\bigcup_{n} \mathbb{F}_{p^n}$.

⚠ An algebraic closure is not "a unique set" but "unique up to isomorphism"; different constructions give $K$-isomorphic fields.

⭐ Existence uses Zorn: take the partially ordered set of all algebraic extensions; a maximal element must be algebraically closed (otherwise adjoin one more root and continue).
